life-insurance.title: Life insurance
life-insurance.information:
Mortgage life insurance pays out a lump sum to cover your outstanding mortgage debt if you die.

Check your policy details or your bank statement to find out exactly what your monthly premiums are.

If you haven't checked your policy lately you might find that it's worth shopping around. Find out more in our guide:

[What is life insurance?](https://www.moneyhelper.org.uk/en/everyday-money/insurance/what-is-life-insurance)

protection-insurance.title: Income protection insurance
protection-insurance.information:
Income protection insurance pays a percentage of your income if you can't work because you're ill or injured.

Check your policy details or your bank statement to find out exactly what your monthly premiums are.

If you're not sure whether the policy you have is right for you or good value for money, see our guide: [What is income protection insurance?](https://www.moneyhelper.org.uk/en/everyday-money/insurance/what-is-protection-insurance)

critical-illness-insurance.title: Critical illness insurance
critical-illness-insurance.information:
Critical illness insurance pays out a lump sum if you get one of the specific medical conditions or injuries listed on your policy.

It's often sold alongside your mortgage.

Check your policy details or your bank statement to find out exactly what your monthly premiums are.

If you're not sure whether the policy you have is right for you or good value for money, see our guide: [What is critical illness cover?](https://www.moneyhelper.org.uk/en/everyday-money/insurance/what-is-critical-illness-cover)

health-insurance.title: Health insurance
health-insurance.information:
This is sometimes known as private medical insurance.

Check your policy details or your bank statement to find out exactly what your monthly premiums are.

If you have health insurance as part of your benefits package from work there is no need to include a figure here because your employer pays your premium for you.

dental-insurance.title: Dental insurance
dental-insurance.information:
This could be either an insurance policy or what's known as a 'capitation plan' (eg Denplan, which spreads the cost of treatment over the year).

Check your paperwork or your bank statement to find out exactly what your monthly payments are.

Double check 'Dental care' on the Living costs page to make sure you haven't entered the same figure twice.

overdraft-charges-interest.title: Overdraft charges & interest
overdraft-charges-interest.information:
You should be able to see the monthly interest and fees charged on your overdraft by checking your bank statements.

Look at what you've been charged over the past few months and select the correct frequency from the dropdown so that the tool calculates your monthly average for you.

If you often go overdrawn you should consider switching to an account that has a fee-free overdraft and/or a low interest rate. Find out more: [How to choose the right bank account](https://www.moneyhelper.org.uk/en/everyday-money/banking/how-to-choose-the-right-bank-account)

bank-account-fees.title: Bank account fees
bank-account-fees.information:
If you have an account that charges a monthly or an annual fee, enter the amount here.

If this seems high and you want to shop around for an account that is more suitable for you, see our guide: [How to choose the right bank account](https://www.moneyhelper.org.uk/en/everyday-money/banking/how-to-choose-the-right-bank-account)

penalties.title: Penalties
penalties.information:
You might be charged penalties for an unauthorised overdraft or for refused payments (for example if there's not enough money in your account to cover a payment).

Look at what you've been charged over the past few months and select the correct frequency from the dropdown so that the tool calculates your monthly average for you.

If you have a lot of penalties to pay you could consider switching to an account that is more suited to your situation. Find out more in our guide: [How to choose the right bank account](https://www.moneyhelper.org.uk/en/everyday-money/banking/how-to-choose-the-right-bank-account)

loan-repayments.title: Loan repayments
loan-repayments.information:
If you're employed, your repayments are taken automatically from your salary. You can find the exact amount on your payslip.

If you're self-employed, you repay your student loan through your annual Self Assessment tax return.

Find out more in our guide [How to deal with debts after graduation](https://www.moneyhelper.org.uk/en/family-and-care/student-and-graduate-money/how-to-deal-with-debts-after-graduation-from-university).

student-loan-repayments.title: Student loan repayments
student-loan-repayments.information:
If you're employed, your repayments are taken automatically from your salary. You can find the exact amount on your payslip.

If you're self-employed, you repay your student loan through your annual Self Assessment tax return.

Find out more in our guide [How to deal with debts after graduation](https://www.moneyhelper.org.uk/en/family-and-care/student-and-graduate-money/how-to-deal-with-debts-after-graduation-from-university).

credit-card-repayments.title: Credit card repayments
credit-card-repayments.information: If you clear your balance every month you can leave this box blank. Otherwise, check your credit card statements to see what your monthly repayments are.

car-hire-payments.title: Car hire purchase payments
car-hire-payments.information:
Check your paperwork or your bank statement to find out exactly what your monthly repayments are.

Why not see if you could cut the cost of your borrowing? See our guide: [Bill prioritiser](https://www.moneyhelper.org.uk/en/money-troubles/cost-of-living/bill-prioritiser)

buy-now-pay-later.title: Buy now, pay later payments
buy-now-pay-later.information: Enter the amount you pay regularly for purchases made through schemes like Klarna, Clearpay or PayPal, or if you have more than one, put it into Your additional items.

other-credit-repayments.title: Other credit repayments
other-credit-repayments.information: Enter the amount you pay regularly for any other credit not listed above, such as store cards, catalogue credit or hire purchase agreements, or if you have more than one, put it into Your additional items.

regular-saving.title: Regular saving
regular-saving.information:
Enter the amount here that you regularly put aside either weekly or monthly into a savings account or similar.

If you regularly put money into a savings account in someone else's name - for example your children - include that here too.

lump-sum-savings.title: Lump sum savings
lump-sum-savings.information: Enter here any amounts that you put into an ISA account. Be sure to choose the correct frequency – for example, year or month – from the dropdown menu. If you put money into a Junior ISA for your child, include that here too.

payments-isas.title: Payments into ISAs
payments-isas.information: Enter here any amounts that you put into an ISA account. Be sure to choose the correct frequency - for example, year or month - from the dropdown menu. If you put money into a Junior ISA for your child, include that here too.

buying-shares.title: Buying shares & other investments
buying-shares.information: If you put money into investments, for example, shares or bonds, enter the amount you invest here. Be sure to choose the correct frequency - for example, year or month - from the dropdown menu.

private-pensions.title: Private pension contributions
private-pensions.information: If your pension contributions are deducted from your pay then you should leave this box blank. However, if you're investing in your own private pension scheme, this is where you should put your contributions.

long-term-care.title: Long term care plan
long-term-care.information: If you're paying a fixed monthly payment into an insurance policy to fund your future long-term care then enter the premium here.

funeral-plan.title: Funeral plan
funeral-plan.information: If you're paying regular instalments or a fixed monthly payment into a funeral plan enter the amount you pay here.

financial-advice.title: Financial & legal advice
financial-advice.information: If you pay fees for a financial adviser, or a legal professional, enter the amount here.
